scope: Available single-board, single-access-point physical provisioning matrix on signed firmware sequence 5 and the isolated LAN deployment

physicalCases.case: owner-preserving visible-network change through the shared TypeScript client
physicalCases.finding: BLE completion became uncertain while the radio changed state; a new Security2 session confirmed the saved network, owner binding, epoch and native presence without resending credentials.
The board accepted apply_hidden without a scan index or BSSID pin; secure resume confirmed the existing owner and native presence.
After a deliberately invalid candidate credential, the board returned through the previous saved network and retained its owner epoch and native presence.
Chrome paired with the physical board, completed Security2, and rendered the robot-originated scan with incompatible networks disabled.
A scan older than 30 seconds was rejected before credential application. After refresh, BLE loss produced the Resume setup action; a new Chrome pairing reached the visible success state.

limitations: Only one physical access point was available, so different-location and laptop-only-AP isolation were not physically demonstrated.
The original 19-of-20 setup and 19-of-20 network-change rate gates were not rerun on this sequence.
Arbitrary power cuts at every commit boundary, full physical reset, offline unlink/relink and five-participant usability remain separate acceptance work.
The localhost bridge was a loopback-only test adapter that preserved upstream TLS verification; production deployment still requires a browser-trusted HTTPS certificate.
